lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details that should be removed.
items.because: A reader is not meant to weigh them, and they take space without supporting the candidate’s qualifications.

items.says: The experience section is not in newest-first order.
items.because: Brightcart ended later than Pinecrest, so listing Pinecrest first makes the chronology harder to scan.

items.says: The daily p-value checks and stop rule do not support treating the result as significant at the usual 0.05 level.
items.because: Stopping at the first p-value below 0.05 increases the false-positive rate, and no correction or prespecified stopping rule is described.

items.says: The bullet gives no test outcome or impact, while process detail takes space from the result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the test established or whether it improved checkout performance.

items.says: The entry’s strongest accomplishment is not its opening bullet.
items.because: Readers encounter the checkout-test bullet before the concrete call-center result.

items.says: The line does not say how the analysis identified the evening peak.
items.because: A reader cannot see what analytical skill led to the staffing decision.

items.says: The first-person pronoun does not belong in this résumé bullet.
“Writes” conflicts with the role’s July 2022 end date.
items.because: The present tense reads as a current responsibility, but the role has ended.

items.says: The list of secondary duties buries the fraud extract’s time-saving result.
items.because: A scanning reader may reach the end before seeing the result, and the other duties do not clarify the extract’s value.

items.says: The Pinecrest entry mixes analysis, process work, a statistical test, and support duties without a clear picture of the analyst’s work.
The dashboard bullet does not show the analytical logic used to define the retargeting audience.
items.because: A reader cannot see what analysis went into identifying lapsed buyers.

items.says: The described join and null check do not identify customers with no orders.
items.because: An orders-left join excludes those customers, while a customers-left join does not make the preserved customer name null.

items.says: The bullet does not say what the finding enabled or changed.
The finding gives no measure of how many customers had no orders.
The campaign-attribution result is buried after a long methods list.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters several method details before the outcome.

items.says: The bullet does not describe the analysis behind the funded recommendations.
items.because: A reader cannot see what analytical work informed them.

items.says: The percentage error is undefined, with no evaluation period or split identified.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the accuracy without knowing what the percentage is relative to or what period it covers.

items.says: The line does not identify the forecasting approach.
items.because: The tools in the project heading do not show the model or approach used.

items.says: Past-tense “Modeled” conflicts with the ongoing project and present-tense “forecasting.”
The decrease from 300 to 200 hours is a 33.3% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: The 100-hour decrease divided by the original 300 hours is 33.3%.

items.says: The line does not identify the comparison rebalancing schedule or approach.
items.because: Without the baseline, a reader cannot tell what the replay changed or how to interpret the reduction.

items.says: The change from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, not a 15% relative increase.
items.because: Relative to the original 60% hit rate, the increase is 25%.

items.says: “Hit” is undefined.
items.because: A reader cannot assess what the metric counts.

items.says: The line does not state the number of unique households identified.
The monthly use of the guide has no stated duration.
